js.networks.cap.name: Name
js.networks.capd.name: The name of each device
js.networks.capd.mac: The physical address of each device
js.networks.capd.quiet: The devices that do not answer
js.networks.capd.stray: The devices with an address of another network
js.networks.how.pres.lead: Vedetta always sees who is on.
js.networks.how.name.lead: The router does not share the names of the devices of this network.
js.networks.how.mac.lead: The MAC of the devices does not cross the router.
js.networks.how.port.lead: The router blocks the checks of Vedetta towards this network.
js.networks.how.deep.lead: Brand and model travel in the mDNS announcements, which the router stops.
js.networks.how.quiet.lead: Devices that do not answer can be seen only from inside the network.
js.networks.how.stray.lead: Devices with a wrong address can be heard only from inside the network.
js.networks.way.router_integration.title: Add the router integration
js.networks.way.router_integration.what: Search for the brand of the router and sign in. Home Assistant reads the list of clients the router knows.
js.networks.way.router_integration.sec: Home Assistant keeps the access to the router. Use a read-only user, if the router has one.
js.networks.way.ha_inside.title: Connect Home Assistant to this network
js.networks.way.ha_inside.what: With a second network card: set its address here.
js.networks.ui.inside_vlan: With a VLAN: create it first from the Home Assistant Terminal, then set it here.
js.networks.way.ha_inside.sec: The devices of this network will be able to reach Home Assistant. Avoid it for the guest network and for devices you do not trust.
js.networks.way.firewall_rule.title: Let Home Assistant reach the network
js.networks.way.firewall_rule.what: New rule: source {from}, destination {to}, action Allow.
js.networks.way.firewall_rule.sec: Use only the address of Home Assistant as the source. Traffic from this network towards home stays blocked.
js.networks.way.router_dns.title: Register the names in the router's DNS
js.networks.way.router_dns.what: Turn on the registration of the names of the DHCP clients.
js.networks.way.snmp.title: Turn on read-only SNMP v2c
js.networks.way.snmp.what: Write here the router's address and the community: Vedetta will read the table of MACs from the router.
js.networks.way.snmp.sec: Allow only the address of Home Assistant and use a community just for Vedetta: v2c sends it in clear text.
js.networks.way.mdns_reflector.title: Forward the mDNS announcements
js.networks.way.mdns_reflector.what: Turn on the forwarding between the network of Home Assistant and this one.
js.networks.way.mdns_reflector.sec: Only the announcements pass, not the traffic. Do not turn it on towards the guest network.
js.networks.ui.title: Networks
js.networks.ui.all_sub: Ignored by name, or by MAC with no known address.
js.networks.ui.link_direct: Home Assistant is inside this network
js.networks.ui.routed_note: Devices here are found by ping, every 15 minutes. Without the router integration in Home Assistant, a device that changes address looks new.
js.networks.ui.vlan_hint: Optional: the VLAN number in the router.
js.networks.ui.danger_text: Deletes this network and everything Vedetta knows about it.
js.networks.ui.confirm_text: If a device of this network comes back to the list, the network comes back as new.
js.networks.ui.confirm_counts: It deletes devices in the list: {cards} · MAC addresses seen: {devices} · history rows: {rows}.
js.networks.ui.confirm_ignored: And entries of the ignored list (by MAC or address): {ignored}.
js.networks.ui.danger_main_text: Deletes all the devices of this network and what Vedetta knows about them. The network stays.
js.networks.ui.confirm_main_text: Then Vedetta starts over as at the first install: what it finds next is the starting point, with no new-device alerts.
js.networks.ui.cidr_hint: You find it in the router, under LAN or VLAN.
js.networks.ui.add_note: First Vedetta tries it: one ping to each address. Nothing is saved.
js.networks.ui.testing: Trying: one ping to each address, up to half a minute.
js.networks.ui.test_none: No address answers the ping. You can add it anyway.
js.networks.ui.later_how: Can be turned on after adding
js.networks.ui.later_off: Off: you can switch it on after adding
js.networks.ui.load_failed: The networks could not be read.
js.networks.ui.foot_done: When you are done, the function turns on by itself.
js.networks.ui.foot_menus: Menu names change from one router to another: if in doubt, check the manual. Vedetta changes neither the router nor Home Assistant.
js.networks.snmp.bad_router: Write the private address of your router, for example 192.168.1.1
js.networks.snmp.bad_community: The community is one line, 64 characters at most
js.networks.snmp.off: Write the address and the community first
